title: Torus-stable additive series in a split unipotent group over an arbitrary field
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field]. All groups are affine $k$-group schemes of finite type [def-sc-group-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and subgroups are closed subgroup schemes [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. Smoothness and connectedness have the meanings of [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme]; geometrically connected means connected after every field extension. Let $U$ be smooth and geometrically connected and split unipotent: there is a faithful finite-dimensional matrix representation in which all geometric points are unipotent matrices, and a finite descending series of smooth geometrically connected subgroups, each normal in its predecessor, with represented fppf quotients isomorphic to $\mathbf G_a$ [def-sc-gm-ga]. A represented fppf quotient is the group scheme representing the sheafification of the right-coset functor for faithfully flat finitely presented coverings of commutative $k$-algebras. Let $E=\mathbf G_{m,k}^s$, $s\geq0$, act on $U$ by $k$-group automorphisms: a morphism $E\times_kU\to U$ obeying the unit, associativity and group-homomorphism identities. Then there are $m\geq0$ and a descending series $U=V_0\supseteq V_1\supseteq\cdots\supseteq V_m=1$ of smooth geometrically connected subgroups normal in $U$ and stable under $E$, with $k$-group isomorphisms $b_i:V_i/V_{i+1}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf G_a$ for $0\leq i<m$, such that for some $n_i=(n_{i1},\ldots,n_{is})\in\mathbf Z^s$ the induced $E$-action on each quotient satisfies
$$b_i(e\cdot\bar v)=\left(\prod_{j=1}^s e_j^{n_{ij}}\right)b_i(\bar v)$$
on every commutative $k$-algebra. In particular the quotient homomorphism $q_i:V_i\to\mathbf G_a$ defined by $b_i$ has scheme-theoretic kernel $V_{i+1}$. If $U=1$, $m=0$ is allowed. There is no perfectness, infinitude or characteristic restriction on $k$.

source.place: Supporting equivariant filtration for Summary 16.29(d) and Proposition 16.54, printed pp.334,344. This arbitrary-field split-unipotent formulation is an agent-specified structural input, not an application of the perfect-field-only Corollary 16.24. WANTED: Conrad, Linear Algebraic Groups I (Stanford, Winter 2010), Appendix D.3, proof of Theorem D.3.2, printed pp.86–87, invariant vector-group series and linearization of the split-torus actions.

proof.text: Use strong induction on the finite nonnegative integer $\dim U$, proving the stated assertion for every split-torus action and split unipotent group of that dimension. Affineness implies separatedness by the cited lemma. Finiteness and nonnegativity follow from the dimension lemma (take the identity subgroup). If $U=1$, choose $m=0$. For $U\ne1$, the central-vector-subgroup lemma supplies an $E$-stable central $C\simeq\mathbf G_a^d$ with $d\geq1$. Apply vector-group linearization to its restricted action, obtaining an equivariant $a:\mathbb V(W)\simeq C$ and the linear Laurent coaction on the nonzero vector space $W$.

proof.text: The normal-quotient lemma constructs $q:U\to Q=U/N$ with kernel $N$, with $Q$ affine, smooth and geometrically connected. The quotient-splitness lemma applies to this smooth geometrically connected central $N$, so $Q$ is split unipotent. The action descends by $e\cdot q(u)=q(e\cdot u)$: stability of $N$ makes this independent of an fppf-local representative, and the represented sheaf quotient gives an algebraic action. The group and action identities descend from those on $U$. The dimension lemma gives $\dim U=\dim N+\dim Q$, and $\dim N\geq1$ since $k[z]$ has the strict prime chain $(0)\subsetneq(z)$. Thus $\dim Q<\dim U$ and the induction hypothesis applies to $Q$ with this $E$-action.

proof.text: Write the resulting quotient series as $Q=W_0\supseteq\cdots\supseteq W_r=1$. Put $V_i=q^{-1}(W_i)$ for $0\leq i\leq r$, and append $V_{r+1}=1$. The normal-quotient lemma makes every $V_i$ smooth and connected, normal in $U$, and identifies $V_i/V_{i+1}$ with $W_i/W_{i+1}$ for $i<r$. The same argument after every field extension gives geometric connectedness, since quotient formation commutes with that extension and $N_K,W_{i,K}$ are connected. Equivariance of $q$ proves $E$-stability. The quotient isomorphisms respect $E$: locally lift a section to $V_i$ and use $q(e\cdot v)=e\cdot q(v)$; equality of the sheaf maps is checked fppf locally. Transport the character parameters from the quotient series along these isomorphisms. Finally $V_r=\ker q=N$ and $V_r/V_{r+1}=N$ has parameter $b$ and weight $\nu$. This also covers $Q=1$ and $r=0$. Each final homomorphism to $\mathbf G_a$ is a quotient map followed by an isomorphism, so its scheme-theoretic kernel is exactly $V_{i+1}$ by the normal-quotient lemma. This completes the induction.
